title: app-01: Niri layout parity audit
summary: Catalogare gap di comportamento/animazione rispetto a Niri e validare column width reflow.
description:
═══ THE THREE OPEN ITEMS, RESCUED FROM PLAN.md (2026-07-26) ═══
From the 2026-06-17/18 compatibility re-check. The keybinding complaints were mostly fixed by the
registry rewrite; these three remain.

LESSON RECORDED THERE, WORTH KEEPING: one claim ("focus-up jumps workspaces") was tested and proved
FALSE. Verify behaviour by RUNNING it, not by reading a code path.

1. CATALOGUE EVERY ANIMATION, for a future animation overhaul.
   Write down the full set of motions niri animates and how — open, close, move, resize,
   workspace-switch, view-scroll, overview. niri gives each its own spring/easing config and an off
   switch. Then map each to what heca does today: heca appears to use one simple easing for
   everything, with no spring physics, no per-motion config, and no way to turn animations off.
   The deliverable of this task is the catalogue and gap list. The improvement itself is later work.

2. CONFIRM WHETHER ADDING OR REMOVING A COLUMN ACTUALLY RESIZES THE OTHERS.
   heca recomputes all column widths on every layout change — `update_all_column_widths()` runs on
   every mutation in `heca-core/src/layout/scrolling.rs`. niri never resizes existing columns when
   you open a new one. The open question is whether heca's recompute really changes existing widths
   at runtime or just re-derives the same numbers.
   TEST IT LIVE: resize a column, add and remove another, resize the window — does the first column
   keep its size? If it reflows, switch to storing each column's width and recomputing only the
   changed one.
   ⚠️ This blocks mouse divider-resize (F006): it is unverified whether a manual resize persists or
   gets recomputed away, and divider-drag would feel broken either way until this is settled.

3. RE-AUDIT THE COMPAT ITEMS STILL MARKED "UNVERIFIED" in niri-compatibility-review.md:
   prefix-mode timeout · whether modifiers are read from the event or from a cache · sending a
   literal prefix key through to the terminal · the viewport/chrome coordinate math · the
   single-animation model · the column-width double-caching.
   Go through each against current code, run it where behaviour matters, and update the review's
   status table.

REFERENCE: `niri-compatibility-review.md` + `docs/niri-wiki/` — keep both, do NOT delete. The review
itself needs updating to reflect current heca (flagged 2026-06-17).

tasks.title: A terminal has a minimum size only while you drag a divider — when the WINDOW shrinks, chrome keeps its width and the terminal takes the whole loss
tasks.description:
REPORTED by Antonio 2026-08-25 with a screenshot: two sidebars at their normal width, the window narrowed, and the terminal column reduced to an ~40pt strip with the shell prompt wrapping one or two characters per line. His words: *"there was a rule. terminal cannot be shrinked below a certain number in height and width. Seems to be lost."*

**NOT A REGRESSION, and not lost — it was never enforced on this path.** Evidence, not inference:
- `heca-core/src/layout/scrolling.rs`:11 defines `MIN_COLUMN_WIDTH = 150.0`, and every use of it (:605, :609, :634) is inside the **mouse-resize** path. `git log -S MIN_COLUMN_WIDTH` names only older resize/exposé commits; nothing removed a use.
- `Column::resolve_width` (`heca-core/src/layout/column.rs`:84) has **no floor** for the common case: `ColumnWidth::Proportion(p) => (working_width - gaps) * p - gaps`. Shrink `working_width` and the column follows it to nothing.
- `MIN_PANE_HEIGHT = 100.0` (`column.rs`:7) *is* applied in `compute_pane_sizes` (:175-178) but deliberately degrades — `MIN_PANE_HEIGHT.min(available_height / pane_count).max(1.0)` — so it yields the same way vertically.
- **Nothing sets a window minimum**: `min_inner_size` appears nowhere in `heca/src`.
- The layout that squeezed here is the WM's scrolling engine (`heca-core`), which never goes through grid-ui's taffy — so F003/P082/T481's layout rule cannot reach it. This branch's only `heca-core` commit is `d465478`, deleting the dormant overview.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE A LOST RULE
The sidebars are **fixed** widths (`AppState::{left,right}_sidebar_width` → `chrome_state.{left,right}_size()`, `heca/src/app_state.rs`:1033-1047, defaulting to `chrome::DEFAULT_SIDEBAR_WIDTH`). The working area is the window minus those, so as the window narrows the chrome keeps every pixel it had and the terminal absorbs the entire loss. The floor a user *feels* — dragging a divider — is real, which is why its absence here reads as a rule that broke.

WHAT TO BUILD — decide the rule first, it is a policy question
1. **Chrome yields before content does.** The working area is clamped to a floor (`MIN_COLUMN_WIDTH` + gaps wide, `MIN_PANE_HEIGHT` tall); below that the sidebars shrink toward their rail/hidden state instead of holding their width. This is the rule that matches what Antonio expects, and it belongs where the working area is computed, not in each consumer.
2. **The window refuses to get that small** — set `min_inner_size` at window creation (`heca/src/app/startup.rs`) to chrome + one minimum column. Cheap, belt-and-braces, and currently missing entirely. It does NOT replace (1): a sidebar can be widened by drag at any window size.
Take both, in that order, unless Antonio says otherwise.

EDGE CASES
- Both sidebars visible AND wide by drag: (1) must still leave a terminal, so the yield order needs a rule (last-resized first? both proportionally?).
- A workspace with several columns: the floor is per *visible* column, and the scrolling engine already scrolls what does not fit — do not turn a scroll into a squeeze.
- Zoomed / full-width columns take `(working_width - gaps*2).max(50.0)` (`column.rs`:86) — that 50 is a second, smaller floor, and should agree with whatever (1) settles on.

VERIFY
Unit: shrinking the working area never resolves a column below the floor; a column count too large for the width scrolls rather than squeezing. Then Antonio: narrow the window hard with both sidebars open and confirm the terminal stops rather than becoming a strip.
